Neural Recording Hardware
Neuromechatronics Lab (NML), Carnegie Mellon University | Advisor: Douglas Weber | Graduate Researcher | Sep 2026 – Present
Designed a 32-channel high-density electromyography (HD-EMG) rigid-flex PCB in KiCad, integrating an 8×4 electrode array, 500 mm flex lead, and Omnetics connector.

Projects
Laika Quadruped Robot: Motor-Control Firmware
CMU Robotics Club | Firmware Team Member | Oct 2026 – Present | GitHub: CMU-Robotics-Club/quads_firmware

Brought up four CAN buses to ODrive motor controllers on an STM32H723 (three on-chip FDCAN plus an SPI-attached MCP2518FD), configuring the clock tree and 1 Mbps bit timing to match the ODrive’s 87.5% sample point.
Integrated a 1 kHz PD joint torque controller into the FreeRTOS control loop with bumpless start, an ODrive watchdog feed and a zero-torque dry-run mode, then validated it on a two-joint test leg.
Biosignal-Driven Shared-Autonomy Assistive Manipulation
Independent Project | Jun 2026 – Present | GitHub: jarrod227/emg-shared-autonomy-arm
Built a three-layer shared-autonomy system in ROS 2 (Jazzy) and MoveIt 2, combining three simple user commands with autonomous perception and motion planning.
Ran a fixed-point LDA intent classifier on an STM32F103 (three surface EMG channels, 20 Hz), reaching 93.3–95.1% offline accuracy on held-out electrode applications.
Added event gating and markerless YOLO-based perception, achieving zero false triggers over 10 minutes of normal activity and object localization within ~1 cm.
Head- and Eye-Controlled Cursor via Electrooculography (EOG) and IMU
Rutgers University | Senior Capstone, Mentor: Simiao Niu | Sep 2025 – May 2026 | GitHub: jarrod227/capstone_project
Owned firmware and signal processing for a 5-person hands-free cursor: head motion drives pointer movement, eye movements handle clicks and scrolling.
Designed a dual-channel AD8232 analog front end for EOG and applied Kalman filtering for gyroscope drift correction, bounding pointer drift over 10+ minutes.
Trained an RBF SVM to classify six eye states, reaching 87.0% cross-validation accuracy and ~77% end-to-end task success across 20 trials per action.
Brain-to-Text Speech Decoding for Brain-Computer Interfaces
Rutgers University | Deep Learning Course Project | Apr 2026 – May 2026 | GitHub: jarrod227/brain2text-skipdiphone
Built a full PyTorch pipeline for intracortical speech decoding: bidirectional GRU encoder, diphone CTC decoder (DCoND) with skip-diphone and smoothness losses, and Kaldi WFST decoding.
Ran a five-variant ablation study on the Brain-to-Text '24 benchmark, improving phoneme error rate to 19.75% vs. 20.48% for the baseline.
Found the phoneme-level gain did not carry over: the baseline retained the lowest word error rate (18.07%) with a 5-gram language model; traced the gap to WFST decoding.
